articles.title: Man arrested for possessing imitation firearm at Rochdale Armistice Day event
articles.excerpt: A man in his 50s was arrested for possessing an imitation firearm during a remembrance ceremony in Rochdale town centre.
articles.content_html:
A man in his 50s was arrested for possessing an imitation firearm during an Armistice Day remembrance ceremony in Rochdale town centre on 11 November 2026.

The incident occurred as the community gathered to pay their respects, and police confirmed that no injuries were reported during the event.

The man was taken into custody after police discovered the imitation firearm near the ceremony. Authorities stated that he did not disrupt the remembrance service, which proceeded without incident.

The police are continuing their inquiries into the matter.

A spokesperson for Greater Manchester Police confirmed that the man remains in custody as investigations continue. They reiterated that the safety of the public is their priority and that no one was harmed during the incident.

The police have not yet released further details regarding the man's identity or the specific charges he may face.

articles.title: Rochdale arts leader Parvez Qadir wins This Is Manchester award
articles.excerpt: The founder of Rochdale-based Breaking Barriers has been recognised for making a difference through arts and community work.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale arts leader Parvez Qadir has won the Individual Making a Difference award at the This Is Manchester Awards 2026.

The artistic director and founder of Breaking Barriers received the award at Emirates Old Trafford on Thursday 5 November. His win is listed on the awards organiser’s official winners page.

Qadir established the Rochdale-based production company in 2019. It uses arts and culture to bring people together and create opportunities for communities whose voices are often underrepresented.

In its announcement of the award, Breaking Barriers said it had delivered more than 80 projects and reached nearly 30,000 young people through Theatre in Education programmes. It also reported live audiences of more than 100,000.

Two education programmes featured in Qadir’s nomination. Crossing the Line explores child criminal exploitation and county lines, while Blind Side addresses violence against women and girls. The company says both aim to help young people recognise harmful behaviour and feel able to speak up.

Qadir said: “My vision has always been to build an organisation that uses creativity as a tool for social change. I believe the arts have a unique power to reach people of all ages in ways that other interventions cannot, to spark conversations that change attitudes and to give communities the confidence to speak up and take action.”

He added: “That is what Breaking Barriers was built to do, and to be recognised for that work here in Greater Manchester is something I am incredibly proud of.”

For Rochdale, the award brings recognition to a locally founded organisation working with residents, artists and young people. Its work includes accessible projects rooted in local places and communities.

articles.title: Middleton man charged with attempted murder and three aggravated burglaries
articles.excerpt: A 33-year-old man from the Middleton area is due before Manchester Magistrates' Court following charges relating to alleged incidents in Oldham.
articles.content_html:
A man from the Middleton area has been charged with attempted murder and three aggravated burglaries following an investigation into alleged incidents in Oldham.

Greater Manchester Police named him as Olatunbosn Sulaimon, 33, in a statement issued on Wednesday 11 November.

The force said he was due to appear at Manchester Magistrates' Court that day.

Two of the aggravated burglary charges relate to alleged incidents in February 2026. The third concerns an alleged incident in October.

The attempted murder charge relates to a man in his 70s and the alleged October incident, according to police.

GMP said it was not seeking any further suspects in connection with these alleged offences.

The charges are allegations. No finding of guilt should be inferred, and the defendant is presumed innocent unless and until convicted.

articles.title: Man who died in Baguley Crescent flat fire in Middleton named as David Mills, 67
articles.excerpt: David Steven Mills died at the scene of a fire in his first-floor flat on Saturday 7 November. Police say there are no suspicious circumstances.
articles.content_html:
The man who died in a fire at a first-floor flat on Baguley Crescent in Middleton on Saturday afternoon has been named as David Steven Mills, 67.

Mr Mills died at the scene despite the efforts of firefighters and paramedics. Greater Manchester Police said there are believed to be no suspicious circumstances.

Emergency services were called to the block shortly after 2.30pm on Saturday 7 November.

Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service sent three fire engines, from Blackley, Whitefield and Broughton. Firefighters wearing breathing apparatus used two hose reels to put the fire out.

Police and North West Ambulance Service also attended.

A Greater Manchester Police spokesperson said: "Sadly, a man in his 60s passed away at the scene, despite the best efforts from emergency services."

Neighbours described Mr Mills as a kind and helpful man who was well known on the estate.

Margaret Moulding, who lived opposite him, said: "He was a very helpful man. He was very kind and it's very sad."

She added: "He was known as a legend in the community."

Francesca Estasy, who knew him from the estate, said: "When I found out it was Dave, who has been here as long as me, it was really sad."

The cause of the fire has not been released, and police say their investigations are ongoing.

Officers are trying to trace Mr Mills' relatives. Anyone who can help is asked to contact the Police Coroner's Office on 0161 856 8555.

Source: Greater Manchester Police, Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service, and reporting by the Manchester Evening News. Photograph: Greater Manchester Police.

articles.title: Six dental practices in Rochdale borough listed as taking new NHS adult patients
articles.excerpt: NHS listings show six practices accepting new adult patients and eight accepting children. None in Heywood or Littleborough is taking adults.
articles.content_html:
Adults looking for an NHS dentist in Rochdale borough have six practices listed as taking new patients, according to NHS listings checked on 9 November.

Eight practices are listed as taking new child patients. None of the listed practices in Heywood or Littleborough is taking new NHS adult patients.

These practices are listed as accepting new NHS adult and child patients: Crescent Orthodontics and Dental Practice, Rochdale, OL16 1PZ; Edenfield Cosmetic and Dental Care, 386 Edenfield Road, Rochdale, OL12 7NH; One Dental, Rochdale, OL16 1UG; Roch Valley Dental, 23 Roch Valley Way, Rochdale, OL11 4PZ; Urgent Dental Care, Rochdale, OL11 2JG; and Langley Dental Group, 215A Wood Street, Middleton, M24 5RU.

Drake Dental Practice in Rochdale, OL16 1PZ, and DHS Dental Practices at The Phoenix Centre, Heywood, OL10 1LR, are listed as accepting new NHS child patients only.

Kings Dental Centre in Rochdale is listed as taking NHS patients by referral only.

Practices listed as not taking new NHS patients include 518 Dental, Bamford Dental Practice and Deeplish Dental Practice in Rochdale, all five listed practices in Heywood, and MF Dental Care in Littleborough.

Availability changes often, so patients should ring a practice to confirm before travelling.

articles.content_html:
Shaun O’Neill, a former councillor for Healey and firefighter, died on 10 November 2026, prompting tributes from colleagues reflecting on his dedication to public service.

Mr O’Neill served as a Labour councillor and was also a representative for the Fire Brigades Union. Colleagues have expressed their sorrow and shared memories of his commitment to the community.

Councillor Shakil Ahmed described him as 'a truly dedicated public servant who gave so much of his life to serving others.'

Councillor Daniel Meredith remembered Mr O’Neill fondly, stating, 'Shaun was a top bloke, a good friend, and someone whose knowledge and experience were second to none.' He highlighted Mr O’Neill’s passion for public service and his commitment to the working people of Rochdale.

The loss of Shaun O’Neill is felt deeply within the community, with many acknowledging his years of service and advocacy. His contributions as both a firefighter and a councillor have left a lasting impact on the Healey area.

articles.title: Is Rochdale Town Hall haunted?
articles.excerpt: There is no verified evidence that the Town Hall is haunted — but its Victorian courts, an 1883 fire, local poltergeist tales and commercial ghost-hunt events have kept the rumours alive.
articles.summary: There is no verified evidence that the Town Hall is haunted — but its Victorian courts, an 1883 fire, local poltergeist tales and commercial ghost-hunt events have kept the rumours alive.
articles.body:
Short answer: no confirmed haunting has been proved.

Rochdale Town Hall is a Grade I Victorian building with a long, well‑documented civic history; that history — not a stack of authenticated supernatural incidents — is what official records record. The council and the Town Hall’s own conservation pages describe the building’s architect (William Henry Crossland), its opening in 1871, the destructive 1883 fire that brought down the original spire and the major restoration work in the 2020s that reopened previously closed rooms to the public. Those are the facts you can rely on. (Rochdale Borough Council and the Town Hall’s conservation pages do not present any official claims of ghosts.)

So where do the hauntings come from? Two things make the building fertile ground for ghost stories. First, old civic buildings commonly held grim functions: magistrates’ hearings, police business and holding cells have been associated with many town halls across the region, and such associations encourage mobile storytelling about restless spirits. Second, modern interest in the paranormal has been channelled into commercial events. Organisers such as Haunted Happenings advertise overnight “ghost hunts” at Rochdale Town Hall, offering vigils, equipment and guided investigations. Those events are available to book and are the clearest public evidence that people believe the building is worth investigating for ghostly activity — but they are promotions by private operators, not independent, peer‑reviewed proof of anything supernatural.

It is important to separate three things: documented history, local folklore and commercial claims. Documented history (architecture, dates, the 1883 fire, the recent conservation programme) is recorded by the Town Hall and its conservation partners and by national heritage bodies. Local folklore includes older regional tales — Rochdale borough has other well‑known legends and alleged poltergeist cases (for example reported mid‑20th century household disturbances in the Kirkholt area) — but those stories are about people and places across the borough, not verified phenomena inside the Town Hall itself. Commercial claims are where the line blurs: ghost‑hunting companies and enthusiast sites promote investigations and recount experiences, but those accounts are not the same as corroborated evidence assessed by historians or independent investigators.

If you want to check the official record: Historic and civic sources list the building, its architecture and its conservation programme; Rochdale Borough Council and the Town Hall’s visitor pages outline opening times, the recent restoration and the cultural uses of the Great Hall and other rooms. If you want to see the building after dark, private operators run ticketed paranormal events; those operators describe the kinds of activities they run and their booking rules on their commercial pages. Neither the council nor the Town Hall’s official material presents verified sightings, authenticated recordings or formal investigations that demonstrate the presence of spirits.

What this means for locals: you can enjoy the building’s architecture, visit the Great Hall, watch the peregrine falcons nest in the clock tower via the Town Hall webcam, attend a concert or book a wedding there with confidence that the publicly recorded history is well maintained. If you’re tempted by a ghost hunt, treat it as an experience — a themed night in an atmospheric historic setting — rather than settled proof. Where claims are important to people (for example, allegations of harm or historical abuse) always rely on official findings; nothing we found links such matters to hauntings at the Town Hall.

If you’d like to follow up: the Town Hall’s official history and conservation information are the best starting point; the council’s events and visitor pages give current opening arrangements and services. For those curious about local folklore beyond the Town Hall, compiled reports and archives record several separate local poltergeist and haunting tales — interesting as social history, but not evidence of an institutional haunting in the Town Hall itself.

In short: the Town Hall’s drama is historical and architectural. The ghosts are, so far as the record shows, a matter of local legend, private experience and commercial entertainment, not established public fact.

articles.title: Heywood Christmas Toy Appeal seeks donations to support families in need
articles.excerpt: The Christmas Toy Appeal, organised by local council staff, aims to provide gifts for children living in poverty in Heywood and surrounding areas.
articles.content_html:
The Heywood Christmas Toy Appeal is calling on residents to donate toys and gifts to support local families in need this festive season.

Organised by council staff, the appeal has been running for thirteen years and aims to ensure that children living in poverty have presents to unwrap on Christmas morning.

Donations are being accepted until 11 December, with collection points set up at local libraries and leisure centres. Last year, the appeal successfully distributed 10,000 toys to around 3,000 children, highlighting the significant impact it has on the community.

Helen Walton, a council representative, emphasised the importance of donations, stating that every contribution, regardless of size, is appreciated. Requests for assistance have already begun to come in this year, indicating a continued need for support among local families facing financial pressures.

Councillor Rachel Massey has voiced her support for the appeal, underscoring its role in addressing poverty in the borough.

The Christmas Toy Appeal not only provides festive cheer but also encourages community involvement and kindness, making a real difference in the lives of those who need it most.

articles.title: Shortlist announced for Raising Rochdale Education Awards 2026
articles.excerpt: The shortlist for the Raising Rochdale Education Awards 2026 has been revealed, celebrating local educators for their contributions to children's lives.
articles.content_html:
The shortlist for the Raising Rochdale Education Awards 2026 has been announced, recognising the contributions of local educators.

The awards ceremony will take place on Friday, 20 November 2026, at Rochdale Town Hall, celebrating the achievements of teachers, tutors, and support staff who support children and young people.

This year, the event has received a record 896 nominations, reflecting the growing recognition of local educational professionals.

Eighteen awards will be presented, including categories such as Raising Rochdale School or College of the Year, Leadership Team of the Year, Primary Teacher of the Year, Secondary Teacher of the Year, and Post-16 Tutor of the Year.

Andrew Bridson, headteacher of Cardinal Langley RC High School and event organiser, expressed enthusiasm for the event, stating, "We are thrilled to celebrate the incredible work of our educators who make a difference every day in the lives of our children."

The winners will be announced in front of an audience filled with local education professionals, sponsors, family, and friends.

The Raising Rochdale Education Awards, now in its third year, aims to highlight the achievements of those in the education sector and foster a sense of community pride in local schools.

articles.title: Rochdale Boroughwide Housing ranks in top 25% for tenant satisfaction
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Boroughwide Housing has been recognised for its high tenant satisfaction, ranking among the top landlords in England according to recent government measures.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) has been ranked among the top 25% of landlords in England for tenant satisfaction, according to national results released by the Government and the Regulator of Social Housing (RSH).

The Tenant Satisfaction Measures, which assess how well social landlords deliver services to residents, revealed that RBH achieved an overall satisfaction rate of 80.5%, significantly higher than the national average of 74.2%.

Satisfaction with RBH's repairs service was particularly notable, at 85.2%, compared to the national average of 76%.

RBH has pledged to continue improving its services, with a focus on 'being the best landlord it can be'. A spokesperson for RBH stated, "We are proud of our ranking and will strive to enhance our services further to meet the needs of our tenants."

This recognition comes as part of a broader initiative to ensure social housing providers are held accountable for their service delivery. The results of the Tenant Satisfaction Measures are intended to encourage landlords to improve their performance and better meet the needs of their tenants.

articles.title: Six-week electrical training course opens to unemployed adults in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Training has places on two six-week programmes starting in December and January, with compulsory information sessions before enrolment.
articles.content_html:
Unemployed adults in Rochdale can apply for a six-week electrical installation course, with groups starting in December and January.

Rochdale Training says places remain on the practical programme at its Fishwick Street centre. Participants will work towards the EAL-accredited Level 3 unit Installation of Electrical Equipment. The offer is for that unit, rather than a complete Level 3 electrical installation qualification.

The first group starts on Tuesday 1 December 2026. Applicants must first attend an information session on Wednesday 25 November, from 9.30am to 12.30pm.

The second group begins on Tuesday 26 January 2027, following an information session on Wednesday 13 January, also from 9.30am to 12.30pm. Attendance at an information session is compulsory before a place can be offered.

According to the supplied course flyer, teaching takes place on Tuesdays and Wednesdays from 9.30am to 2.30pm over six weeks, at Rochdale Training, Fishwick Street, Rochdale, OL16 5NA.

The programme covers safe working practices, choosing cables and wiring systems, installing and connecting equipment, following technical requirements, inspection and testing, and commissioning. The provider also says learners will receive careers guidance and support with progression during and after the course.

Applicants must be aged 19 or over, unemployed and living in Rochdale, Oldham or Bury. The recruitment email says they must have lived in the UK for at least three years, must not be enrolled in other training, including ESOL, and must not already hold a Level 3 qualification in electrical installation or a similar subject.

Rochdale Training will check eligibility before offering a place. The announcement does not specify the cost of this particular course, so applicants should confirm any fees or funding arrangements when booking.

For local residents considering a move into engineering, the course offers practical workshop experience and a chance to explore further training, apprenticeships or employment. The announcement does not promise a job on completion.

To ask about eligibility or book an information session, contact Daniel Silva-Stafford at Rochdale Training on 01706 631417 or email dsilva-stafford@rochdaletraining.co.uk. The provider asks applicants who need adjustments or additional support to discuss these before attending.
